*uu, to/, indecl., twenty-third letter of the Formello abecedarium, IG 14.2420 , but twentieth of the Ion. alphabet: as numberal u/ =
400 , but u| =
400 , 000 . It is called to\ u)= by Pl. Cra. 393d , Callias ap. Ath. 10.453d (prob., the line ends tau=, <to\> u)=), IG 22.2783.4
(iv B. C.), Hellad. ap. Phot. Bibl. p.530
B. ; to/ t' u)= or to/ q' u(= might be read in Achae. 33.3 for tou= u_ codd. Ath. ; later to\ u yilo/n or to\ yilo\n u (as name of the first letter of u(/alos, ui(o/s, etc.), Theognost. Can. 18 , Sch. Ar. Pl. 896 , Ps. Hdn. Epim. 116 , 137 , al.: so named to distinguish it from h( o_i_ di/fqoggos, u and oi being pronounced alike in late Gr.; u(= is aspirated in AP 9.385.20 (Steph.Gramm.), 11.67.1 ( Myrin. ) cod.Pal.; the Coptic name
he (cf. Arm.
hiun) may indicate that the early name was u(=, which seems also to be implied by Serv.ad Verg. A. 1.744 :
alii dicunt Hyadas dictas vel ab Y littera, vel a)po\ tou= u(o/s, cf. Sch. Il. 18.486 : the sign Y represents
hy on coins of P. Plautius Hypsaeus ( 58 B.C.), which are inscribed
Ypsae, BMus.Cat.Republ.Coins, Plate
48 Nos. 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , but
Hupsae, Nos. 13 , 14 , Plate 123 Nos. 7 , 8 , 9 .

Ar. 1.19 , Exc. 2 , Theo Sm. p.75 H., etc.; and so u(pepimerh/s is the reciprocal of e)pimerh/s,
